newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state Supreme Court upholds ballpark bonds.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state Supreme Court upholds ballpark bonds.

text.p: Washington state's Supreme Court put construction of a new ballpark for the Seattle Mariners back on track Friday, upholding the January sale of $336 million of bonds for the project.
The court, in a 7-to-2 ruling, rejected the arguments of stadium critics, who argued that the public financing represented an unconstitutional give-away of public funds.

About $336 million of bonds were sold in January by King County, Wash., to finance the $414 million retractable-roof stadium, but the bond funds were placed in escrow pending the Supreme Court ruling.

The ruling was issued one day after the stadium authority put project construction on hold for lack of money. The court decision will release the bond proceeds from escrow, allowing the project to move forward.
The Mariners are hoping to play the second half of the 1999 season in the new ballpark.
After hearing of the Supreme Court decision, stadium opponent Chris Van Dyk, a spokesman for the group Citizens for More Important Things, called off his long fight against the ballpark.
"It is over. The stadium will be built," Van Dyk said.
